title: Hacerse and Volverse: Effort or Character

sections.content: You know *hacerse* from B1 Unit 25 and B1 Unit 39: a change you reach by effort, or with time (*se hizo médico*, *se hace tarde*). You know *volverse* from B1 Unit 39: a deep, lasting change of character (*se volvió desconfiado*). At B2 the difference to learn is who is behind the change. With *hacerse* a person chooses or works towards it: a profession, a belief, a group. That is why it takes a noun: *se hizo abogada*, *se hizo vegetariano*. With *volverse* the change simply happens to the person or the thing, and it takes an adjective: *se volvió egoísta*, *la situación se volvió imposible*. A noun after *volverse* does not work.

sections.title: Choose or happen
rows: Estudió mucho y se hizo abogada.
She studied a lot and became a lawyer. (a profession)
Se hizo vegetariano hace dos años.
He became vegetarian two years ago. (a choice)
Con los años, mi tío se volvió muy desconfiado.
With the years, my uncle became very distrustful. (it happened to him)
El tráfico se ha vuelto imposible.
The traffic has become impossible. (it happened to a thing)

items.spanish: Mi vecina estudió música y se hizo profesora.
items.english: My neighbour studied music and became a teacher.

items.spanish: Desde que cambió de trabajo, se ha vuelto más serio.
items.english: Since he changed jobs, he has become more serious.

items.spanish: Se hizo el sordo cuando le pedí el dinero.
items.english: He pretended not to hear when I asked him for the money.

sections.content: Watch *hacerse el* + adjective: it does not mean "become", it means "pretend to be": *se hizo el sordo*, *se hizo el tonto*. You can use *hacerse* + adjective for a slow change (*se hizo famoso*), but a profession can only follow *hacerse*, never *volverse*: *se hizo médico*, not *se volvió médico*.
